title: Two Runs Short at Lord's. Harmanpreet's Heroics Weren't Enough to Save India's World Cup.
excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur struck 56 off 27 balls in a breathtaking assault, but Australia chased down 171 with six wickets to spare — and India's T20 World Cup campaign is over.
body:
The scoreboard at Lord's read 170 for 4. By the time Australia crossed the line at 172 for 4 in 18.6 overs, India's T20 World Cup was done. A tournament that began with a 64-run demolition of Pakistan ended on a grey London afternoon, two runs the wrong side of history.

Harmanpreet Kaur did everything she could. Walking in at 83 for 2 with India's innings threatening to stall, the captain unleashed one of the most violent cameos of her career — 56 off just 27 deliveries, six fours and three sixes, a strike rate of 207. She retired-hurt Jemimah Rodrigues to give herself more strike in the death overs, and for a few electric minutes at the Home of Cricket, it looked as though sheer force of will might be enough.

It wasn't.

## A Partnership That Set the Stage

India won the toss and chose to bat. The openers — Shafali Verma (34 off 26, with three fours and two sixes) and Smriti Mandhana (38 off 37, six boundaries) — put on 66 for the first wicket in 9.1 overs, laying a platform that should have yielded 180 or more. But left-arm spinner Sophie Molineux disrupted the rhythm, bowling Verma and later removing Harmanpreet in the final over to finish with figures of 4-0-46-2.

Jemimah Rodrigues contributed a measured 34 off 28 before retiring out to allow the power-hitters room. The last two overs produced 23 runs, thanks largely to Harmanpreet's assault, but an extra 10 or 15 might have changed everything.

## The Chase That Ended the Dream

Australia's pursuit was ruthless. With Ellyse Perry anchoring and Ashleigh Gardner accelerating — Perry contributed 33 off 24 balls with four boundaries, while Gardner blazed 27 off 16, including two sixes — the Australians never let the required rate creep above nine.

Deepti Sharma was India's most economical bowler, conceding just 19 off her three overs and picking up a wicket. Renuka Singh also struck, but neither could stem the tide. Australia reached the target with eight balls remaining, finishing on 172 for 4 and sealing their place atop Group A with five wins from five matches.

## What This Means for India

India finish the group stage with three wins and two defeats — losses to South Africa (by six wickets at Old Trafford on June 21) and now Australia at Lord's. Their six points leave them third in Group A, behind Australia (10 points) and South Africa, who secured their semi-final berth earlier in the day by edging Bangladesh 118-117 in a thriller at Lord's.

The elimination stings because this Indian squad arrived in England with genuine pedigree. They won the ODI World Cup in 2025 under Harmanpreet. They swept Australia 2-1 in Australia barely a month ago in a bilateral T20I series. They had beaten Pakistan and the Netherlands convincingly in the group stage. But the loss to South Africa a week earlier meant they arrived at the Australia match with no margin for error — and two runs short is as cruel a margin as any.

## The Diaspora Angle

For NRIs in London and across the UK, this was supposed to be the match. Lord's, the most storied ground in world cricket, hosting India in a virtual quarter-final. Social media buzzed with photos of tri-colour flags in the stands and Bollywood music echoing from the Long Room concourse. Indian-origin fans had traveled from Birmingham, Leicester, and Southall to roar Harmanpreet on.

They got their money's worth from the captain. They just didn't get the result.

## What Comes Next

Harmanpreet Kaur, at 37, has now played her final World Cup match — unless she extends her career to the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, where women's cricket makes its debut. She leaves this tournament averaging over 40 with a strike rate north of 150. The captain led from the front to the very last ball.

The semi-finals are set for July 2 and 3. Australia will play the second-placed team from Group B at The Oval, while the Group A runners-up, South Africa, face the Group B winners. India will watch from outside the ropes — two runs short, and a world away from the trophy they came to win.

*Sources: ICC, ESPNcricinfo, Reuters, SportsCafe*
